questions.q: $If $y = y \left(x\right)$ is the solution of the differential equation \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left($tanx\right)y = sinx, 0 ≤ x \le $\dfrac{π}{3},~with~$y \left($0\right) = 0,$ then y\$left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right)$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(tanx\right)y = sinx; 0 \le x \le \dfrac{π}{3}$

$I . F . = e^{∫ tanxdx} = e^{lnsecx} = secx$

$ysecx = ∫ tanxdx + C$

$ysecx = ln\left|secx\right| + C$

$x = 0, y = 0 ⇒ C = 0$

$ysecx = ln\left|secx\right|$

$y = cosx \cdot ln\left|secx\right|$

${y}_{x = \dfrac{π}{4}} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \cdot ln\sqrt{2}$

questions.q: Let$y = y  \left(x\right)$~be the solution of the differential equation~\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{5}{x\left(x^{5} + 1\right)}$y = $\dfrac{  \left(x^{5} + 1\right)2}{x7},$x > 0$. If $y\left(1\right) = 2$, then~$y\left(2\right)$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{5}{x\left(1 + x^{5}\right)}y = \dfrac{\left(1 + x^{5}\right)2}{x7}$

This is linear differential equation.

$I . F . = e^{∫ \dfrac{5}{x\left(1 + x^{5}\right)}dx}$

$⇒ I . F . = e^{∫ \dfrac{5x^{5}}{x^{6}\left(1 + x^{5}\right)}dx}$

$⇒ I . F . = e^{∫ \dfrac{5}{x^{6}\left(x^{- 5} + 1\right)}dx}$

$⇒ I . F . = e^{- ∫ \dfrac{- 5}{x^{6}\left(x^{- 5} + 1\right)}dx}$

$⇒ I . F . = e^{- ∫ d\left(x^{- 5} + 1\right)\left(x^{- 5} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ I . F . = e^{- \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(x^{- 5} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ I . F . = \left(x^{- 5} + 1\right)- 1 = x^{5}\left(x^{5} + 1\right)$

So, solution is given by

yx^{5} \left($x^{5} + 1\right) = ∫ $x^{5}\left($x^{5} + 1\right)$\times $\dfrac{ \left($x^{5} + 1\right)2}${x7}$dx$

$⇒ yx^{5}\left(x^{5} + 1\right) = ∫ \$left(\dfrac{x^{5} + 1}{x2}\right)$dx$

$⇒ $yx^{5} \left($x^{5} + 1\right) = ∫ \left($x^{3} + \dfrac{1}{x2}\right)dx$

$⇒ $yx^{5}\left($x^{5} + 1\right) = \dfrac{x4}{4} - \dfrac{1}{x} +C$

Since,~y\left($1\right) = 2$, so

$\dfrac{2}{2} = \dfrac{1}{4} -1 + C ⇒ C = \dfrac{7}{4}$

So,

yx^{5}\left($x^{5} + 1\right) = \dfrac{x4}{4} - \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{7}{4}$

Put~$x = 2$, then we get

$\dfrac{y\left(2\right) \times 32}{33} = \dfrac{16}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{7}{4}$

$⇒ $y\left($2\right) = \dfrac{21 \times 33}{128} = \dfrac{693}{128}$

$

questions.q:
$If $y = y \left(x\right), x \in \left($0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right) be the solution curve of the differential equation

\left(\sin^{2}$2x\$right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left($8\sin^{2}2x + 2sin4x\right)y =$

$2e^{- $4x}\left($2sin2x + cos2x\right),$~with $y $\$left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) =$e^{- \pi}$, then $y \left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)$is equal to

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& \left(\sin^{2}2x\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(8\sin^{2}2x + 2sin4x\right)y =$

$2e^{- 4x}\left(2sin2x + cos2x\right)$~

Now rewriting the given~differential equation we get,

$⇒ $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(8 + 4cot2x\right)y = $\dfrac{2e^{- 4x}}{\sin^{2}2x}\left($2sinx + cos2x\right)$

Which is a linear differential~equation.

Now calculating $IF = e^{∫ \left(8 + 4cot2x\right)dx} = e^{8x + 2ln\left(sin2x\right)}$

$= e^{8x} \cdot \sin^{2}2x$

Now solution~of differential equation is given by,

$y \times IF = ∫ $\dfrac{2e^{- 4x}\left(2sin2x + cos2x\right)}{\sin^{2}2x} \times$IFdx$

$⇒ y\left(e^{8x} \cdot \sin^{2}2x\right) = ∫ 2e^{4x}\left(2sin2x + cos2x\right)dx$

$⇒ y\left(e^{8x} \cdot \sin^{2}2x\right) = e^{4x} \cdot sin2x + C$

Now given~$y\$left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) =$e^{- \pi} ⇒ C = 0$

So, the equation of curve is given by~$y = $\dfrac{e- 4x}{sin2x}

So, the value of~$y\$left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) = \dfrac{e- 4\dfrac{π}{6}}{sin\left(2 \cdot \dfrac{π}{6}\right)} = \dfrac{2}{3}$e^{- $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}}$

$

questions.q: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation \left(1+x^2\right) \frac{d y}{d x}+y=e^{\tan ^{-1} x}$, $y(1)=0$. Then $y(0)$ is$

questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{d y}{d x}+\frac{y}{1+x^2}=\frac{e^{\tan ^{-1} x}}{1+x^2} \\ & \text { I.F. }=e^{\int \frac{1}{1+x^2} d x}=e^{\tan ^{-1} x} \\ & y \cdot e^{\tan ^{-1} x}=\int\left(\frac{e^{\tan ^{-1} x}}{1+x^2}\right) e^{\tan ^{-1} x} \cdot d x \\ & \text { Let } \tan ^{-1} x=z \quad \therefore \frac{d x}{1+x^2}=d z \\ & \therefore y \cdot e^z=\int e^{2 z} d z=\frac{e^{2 z}}{2}+C \\ & y \cdot e^{\tan ^{-1} x}=\frac{e^{2 \tan ^{-1} x}}{2}+C \\ & \Rightarrow y=\frac{e^{\tan ^{-1} x}}{2}+\frac{C}{e^{\tan ^{-1} x}}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \because \mathrm{y}(1)=0 \Rightarrow 0=\frac{\mathrme^{\pi / 4}}{2}+\frac{\mathrm{C}}{\mathrme^{\pi / 4}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{C}=\frac{-\mathrme^{\pi / 2}}{2} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{y}=\frac{\mathrme^{\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{x}}}{2}-\frac{\mathrme^{\pi / 2}}{2 \mathrme^{\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{x}}} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{y}(0)=\frac{1-\mathrme^{\pi / 2}}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $f:[1, \infty) \rightarrow[2, \infty)$ be a differentiable function, If $10 \int_1^{\mathrm{x}} f(\mathrm{t}) \mathrm{dt}=5 \mathrm{x} f(\mathrm{x})-\mathrm{x}^5-9$ for all $\mathrm{x} \geq 1$, then the value of $f(3)$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& 10 \frac{\mathrm{~d}}{\mathrm{dx}} \int_1^{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{t}) \mathrm{dt}=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dx}}\left(5 \mathrm{xf}(\mathrm{x})-\mathrm{x}^5-9\right) \\ & \Rightarrow 10 f(x)=5 f(x)+5 \mathrm{xf}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})-5 \mathrm{x}^4 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})+\mathrm{x}^4=\mathrm{xf}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x}) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{y}+\mathrm{x}^4=\mathrm{x} \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}+y\left(-\frac{1}{x}\right)=x^3 \\ & \Rightarrow y e^{\int-\frac{1}{x} d x}=\int x^3 e^{\int-\frac{1}{x} d x}+c \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{ye}^{-\operatorname{tn}|x|}=\int \mathrm{x}^3 \mathrme^{-\operatorname{tr}|x|}+\mathrm{c} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{y}}{|\mathrm{x}|}=\int \frac{\mathrm{x}^3}{|\mathrm{x}|}+\mathrm{c} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}=\int \mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{c} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}=\frac{\mathrm{x}^3}{3}+\mathrm{c}
\end{aligned}$
Put $x=1$ in given equation
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow 0=5 \mathrm{f}(1)-1-9 \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(1)=2 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{2}{1}=\frac{1}{3}+\mathrm{c} \Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=\frac{5}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{f}(3)}{3}=\frac{27}{3}+\frac{5}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(3)=32
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $f  \left(x\right)$ be a differentiable function such that $f^{'}  \left(x\right) = 7 - \dfrac{3}{4}\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x}, \left(x > 0\right)$ and $f  \left($1\right) \ne 4 .$ Then $\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}} ⁡ $xf\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,& $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{3y}{4x} = 7($ where $y = f ( x ) )$

This is a linear differential equation.

Integrating factor,~$I . F .= e^{∫ \dfrac{3dx}{4x}} = e^{\dfrac{3}{4}lnx} = x^{\dfrac{3}{4}}$

So, integrating the given differential equation using $I . F .$~

$⇒ y . x^{\dfrac{3}{4}} = ∫ 7 . x^{\dfrac{3}{4}}dx$

$⇒ y . x^{\dfrac{3}{4}} = 7 . \dfrac{4x^{\dfrac{7}{4}}}{7} + C$

$⇒ y\left(x^{\dfrac{3}{4}}\right) = 4x^{\dfrac{7}{4}} + C$

$⇒ f ( x ) = 4x + Cx^{\dfrac{- 3}{4}}$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}xf\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) ⇒ \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}x\left(\dfrac{4}{x} + Cx^{\dfrac{3}{4}}\right) = 4$

questions.q:
Let& $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation~$cosx\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2ysinx = sin2x, x \in \left($0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right)
If~$y ( $\pi$/ 3 ) = 0,$ then~$y ( $\pi$/ 4 )$ is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2tanx \cdot y = 2sinx$

I.F. $= e^{∫ 2tanxdx} = \sec^{2}x$

solution is
$y \cdot \sec^{2}x = ∫ 2sinx \cdot \sec^{2}xdx + C$

$y\sec^{2}x = 2secx - 4$
$y\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \sqrt{2} - 2$

questions.q:
Let $y = y ( x )$ satisfies the equation~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \left|A\right| = 0,$~for all $x > 0,$ where $A = \left[\begin{cases}y & sinx & 1 \\ 0 & - 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & \dfrac{1}{x}\end{cases}\right]$. If~$y ( \pi ) = \pi + 2,$~then the value of $y \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)is:

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$We have,

$A = \left[\begin{cases}y & sinx & 1 \\ 0 & - 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & \dfrac{1}{x}\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = - \dfrac{y}{x} + 2sinx + 2$

Now,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left|A\right|$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \dfrac{y}{x} + 2sinx + 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = 2sinx + 2$

$\text{I.F.} = e^{∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx} = x$

Solution is

$y \times \left(I . F .\right) = ∫ \left(I . F .\right) \times \left(2sinx + 2\right)dx$

$⇒ yx = ∫ x ( 2sinx + 2 ) dx$

$⇒ yx = 2 ∫ x \left(sinx\right)dx + 2 ∫ xdx$

$⇒ xy = x^{2} - 2xcosx + 2sinx + c \ldots \left(i\right)$

Now~$x = \pi,y = \pi +2$, hence

$⇒ \pi \left(\pi + 2\right) = {π}^{2} - 2\pi\left(- 1\right) + 0 + c$

$⇒ c = 0$

Now \left(i\right)$~becomes

$xy = x^{2} - 2xcosx + 2sinx$

Put~$x = \dfrac{π}{2}$, then

\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)y = \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)2 - 2 \cdot \dfrac{π}{2}cos \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) +2sin \$left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)$y = $\dfrac{\pi2}{4} +$2$

$⇒ y = $\dfrac{π}{2} + \dfrac{4}{π}

$

questions.q: If& $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + e^{x} \left($x^{2} - 2\right)y = \left(x^{2} - 2x\right)  \left(x^{2} - 2\right)e^{2x}$~and~$y\left(0\right) = 0$,~then~the value of~$y\left(2\right)$& is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + e^{x}\left(x^{2} - 2\right)y = \left(x^{2} - 2x\right)\left(x^{2} - 2\right)e^{2x}$

It is linear differential equation so,

$IF = e^{∫ \left(x^{2} - 2\right)e^{x}dx}$

$= e^{x^{2}e^{x} - 2 ∫ xe^{x}dx - 2e^{x}}= e^{x^{2}e^{x} - 2\left[xe^{x} - e^{x}\right] - 2e^{x}}$

$IF = e^{\left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x}}$

Now solution is given by

$y \times e^{\left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x}} = ∫ e^{\left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x}} \times \left(x^{2} - 2x\right)\left(x^{2} - 2\right)e^{2x}$

$= ∫ e^{\left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x}} \times \left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x}\left(x^{2} - 2\right)e^{x}$

Now let \left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x} = t$

We get~$e^{x}\left(x^{2} - 2x\right) + e^{x}\left(2x - 2\right)dx = dt$

$e^{x}\left(x^{2} - 2x + 2x - 2\right)dx = dt$~

$e^{x}\left(x^{2} - 2\right)dx = dt$

$y \times e^{\left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x}} = ∫ e^{t} \times t \times dt$

$y \times e^{\left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x}} = e^{t}\left(t - 1\right) + c$

$y \times e^{\left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x}} = e^{\left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x}}\left(\left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x} - 1\right) + c$

Now at~$x = 0y = 0$

$0 \times e^{0} = e^{0}\left(0xe^{x} - 1\right) + c$

$0 = - 1 + cc = 1$

Putting the value of~$c = 1$~we get the equation as

$⇒ y \times e^{\left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x}} = e^{\left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x}}\left(\left(x^{2} - 2x\right)e^{x} - 1\right) + 1$

Now putting~$x = 2$~in equation we get

$y \times e^{\left(4 - 4\right)e^{2}} = e^{\left(4 - 4\right)e^{2}}\left(\left(4 - 4\right)e^{2} - 1\right) + 1$

$⇒ y \times e^{0} = e^{0}\left(\left(0\right)e^{2} - 1\right) + 1$

$⇒ y = - 1 + 1 = 0$

$

questions.q: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation \left(2 x \log _e x\right) \frac{d y}{d x}+2 y=\frac{3}{x} \log _e x, x \gt 0$ and $y\left(e^{-1}\right)=0$. Then, $y(e)$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{d y}{d x}+\frac{y}{x \ell \ln x}=\frac{3}{2 x^2} \\ & \therefore \text { I.F. }=e^{\int \frac{1}{x \ln x} d x}=e^{\ln (\ln (x))}=\ln x \\ & \therefore y \ell \ln x=\int \frac{3 \ln x}{2 x^2} d x \\ & =\frac{3 \ln x}{2} \int x^{-2} d x-\int\left(\frac{3}{2 x} \cdot \int x^{-2} d x\right) d x \\ & =\frac{3 \ln x}{2}\left(-\frac{1}{x}\right)-\int \frac{3}{2 x}\left(-\frac{1}{x}\right) d x \\ & \text { y. } \ln x=\frac{-3 \ell n x}{2 x}-\frac{3}{2 x}+C\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \because \mathrm{y}\left(\mathrme^{-1}\right)=0 \\ & \therefore 0(-1)=\frac{3 \mathrm{e}}{2}-\frac{3 \mathrm{e}}{2}+\mathrm{C} \Rightarrow \mathrm{C}=0 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{y}=\frac{-3 \ell \mathrm{nx}}{2 \mathrm{x}}-\frac{3}{2 \mathrm{x}} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{y}(\mathrm{e})=\frac{-3}{2 \mathrm{e}}-\frac{3}{2 \mathrm{e}}=\frac{-3}{\mathrm{e}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $f:(0, \infty) \rightarrow \mathbf{R}$ be a function which is differentiable at all points of its domain and satisfies the condition $x^2 f^{\prime}(x)=2 x f(x)+3$, with $f(1)=4$. Then $2 f(2)$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & x^2 f^{\prime}(x)-2 x f(x)=3 \\ & \left(\frac{x^2 f^{\prime}(x)-2 x f(x)}{\left(x^2\right)^2}\right)=\frac{3}{\left(x^2\right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{d}{d x}\left(\frac{f(x)}{x^2}\right)=\frac{3}{x^4}\end{aligned}$ Integrating both sides
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{f(x)}{x^2}=-\frac{1}{x^3}+C \\
& f(x)=-\frac{1}{x}+C x^2 \\
& \text { put } x=1 \\
& 4=-1+C \Rightarrow C=5 \\
& f(x)=-\frac{1}{x}+5 x^2 \\
& \text { Now } 2 \times f(2)=2 \times\left[-\frac{1}{2}+5 \times 2^2\right] \\
& =39
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $If $y = y  \left(x\right)$~is the solution curve of the differential equation \dfrac{dy}{dx} +$ytanx = xsecx, 0 ≤ x \le $\dfrac{π}{3},$y  \left($0\right) = 1$,~then y\$left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)$is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + ytanx = xsecx$

This is a linear differential~equation.

$I . F . = e^{∫ tanxdx} = secx$

Then solution of~differential~equation is

$y\left(secx\right) = ∫ x\sec^{2}xdx$

$⇒ y\left(secx\right) = xtanx - ∫ tanxdx$

$⇒ y\left(secx\right) = xtanx - ln\left(secx\right) + C$

Given:

$y\left(0\right) = 1 ⇒ c = 1$

$∴ y\left(secx\right) = xtanx - ln\left(secx\right) + 1$

At $x = \dfrac{π}{6}$, we get

$y\left(sec\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)\right) = \left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)tan\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) - ln\left(sec\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)\right) + 1$

$⇒ y\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) - ln\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) + 1$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{π}{12} - \dfrac{3}{2}ln\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) + \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{π}{12} - \dfrac{3}{2} \left[ln \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) -$lne\right]$

$⇒ y = $\dfrac{π}{12} - \dfrac{3}{2}\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{2}{e\sqrt{3}}\right)$

questions.q: If $y(x)$ is the solution of the differential equation $\frac{d y}{d x}+\left(\frac{2 x+1}{x}\right) y=e^{-2 x}, x \gt 0,$ where $y(1)=\frac{1}{2} e^{-2},$ then:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: Given differential equation is, $\frac{d y}{d x}+\left(2+\frac{1}{x}\right) y=e^{-2 x}, x \gt 0\mathrm{IF}=e^{\int\left(2+\frac{1}{x}\right) d x}=e^{2 x+\ln x}=x e^{2 x}$ Complete solution is given by $y(x) \cdot x e^{2 x}=\int x e^{2 x} \cdot e^{-2 x} d x+c=\int x d x+cy(x) \cdot e^{2 x} \cdot x=\frac{x^{2}}{2}+c$ Given, $y(1)=\frac{1}{2} e^{-2}\therefore \quad \frac{1}{2} e^{-2} \cdot e^{2} \cdot 1=\frac{1}{2}+c \Rightarrow c=0\therefore \quad y(x)=\frac{x^{2}}{2} \cdot \frac{e^{-2 x}}{x}y(x)=\frac{x}{2} \cdot e^{-2 x}$ Differentiate both sides with respect to $xy^{\prime}(x)=\frac{e^{-2 x}}{2}(1-2 x) \lt 0 \forall x \in  \left(\frac{1}{2},1\right)$ Hence, $y(x)$ is decreasing in $\$left(\frac{1}{2},$1\right)$

\dfrac{dt}{dx} + \dfrac{t}{x} = \dfrac{1}{2x^{2}}

$I . F{=}_e^{∫ $\dfrac{1}{x}$dx} = e^{lnx} = x$

$tx = ∫ $\dfrac{1}{2x^{2}} \cdotxdx +$C$

Using equation \left($1\right)$
$e^{- y}x = \dfrac{1}{2}ℓnx + C$

Given,~y\left($e\right) = 1$

$e^{- y}x = \dfrac{1}{2} (1 + ℓnx )$

Put $x = 1$ then $y$ is $⇒ y = ℓ$n2\text{or}\log_{\mathrm{e}}$2$

questions.q: Let $y = {y}_{1}  \left(x\right)$~and $y = {y}_{2}  \left(x\right)$~be two distinct solutions of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} =x + y$, with ${y}_{1}\left(0\right) = 0$~and ${y}_{2}  \left(0\right) = 1$~respectively. Then, the number of points of intersection of $y = {y}_{1}\left(x\right)$~and $y = {y}_{2}  \left($x\right)$ \text{ and } is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x + y ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = x$

So,~$IF = e^{∫ - 1dx} = e^{- x}$

Now solution is given by~$ye^{- x} = ∫ xe^{- x}dx$

$⇒ ye^{- x} = - xe^{- x} - e^{- x} + c$

$⇒ y = - x - 1 + ce^{x}$

Given,~${y}_{1} \left(0\right) = 0 ⇒ c = 1$

$∴ {y}_{1} = - x - 1 + e^{x} ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Also given~${y}_{2} \left(0\right) = 1 ⇒ c = 2$

$∴ {y}_{2} = - x - 1 + 2e^{x} ⋯ \left(2\right)$

Now from equation~ \left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$~we get, ${y}_{2} - {y}_{1} = e^{x} > 0 ∴ {y}_{2} \ne {y}_{1}$

$∴$~ Number of points of intersection of~${y}_{1}$~and~${y}_{2}$& is zero.

$

questions.q:
Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{ \left(tanx\right) + y}{sinx \left($secx - sinxtanx\right)}, x \in \left($0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right) satisfying the condition $y \left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) =2$. Then, $y\left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right)is

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{tanx + y}{sinx\left(secx - sinxtanx\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{tanx + y}{sinx\left(\dfrac{1}{cosx} - \dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{cosx}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{tanx + y}{sinx\left(\dfrac{\cos^{2}x}{cosx}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{tanx + y}{sinxcosx}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{2y}{sin2x} = \sec^{2}x$

$⇒ IF = e^{- 2 ∫ cosec2xdx}$

$⇒ IF = e^{- log\left|cosec2x - cot2x\right|}$

$⇒ IF = \dfrac{1}{cosec2x - cot2x} = cosec2x + cot2x$

$⇒ IF = \dfrac{1}{sin2x} + \dfrac{cos2x}{sin2x}$

$⇒ IF = \dfrac{2\cos^{2}x}{2sinxcosx}$

$⇒ IF = cotx$

$⇒ y \times cotx = ∫ cotx \times \sec^{2}xdx$

$⇒ y \times cotx = 2 ∫ cosec2xdx$

$⇒ ycotx = log\left|cosec2x - cot2x\right| + c$

Now, using $y\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = 2$ we get,

$⇒ 2cot\dfrac{π}{4} = log\left|cosec\dfrac{π}{2} - cot\dfrac{π}{2}\right| + c$

$⇒ c = 2$

$⇒ ycotx = log \left|$cosec2x - cot2x\right| + 2$

Now, finding $y\left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) we get,

$⇒ ycot$\dfrac{π}{3} =$log\left|$cosec$\dfrac{2\pi}{3} -$cot$\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right| +$2$

$⇒ y $\times \dfrac{1}{3} =$log\left|\dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3}\right| +$2$

$⇒ y $\times \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}$log3 + 2$

$⇒ y = $\dfrac{3}{2}$log3 + 2$\sqrt{3}

$⇒ y = $\sqrt{3} \lleft(log\sqrt{3} +2\right)$

$

questions.q: $Let $y = y ( x )$~be the solution of the differential equation $x^{3}dy + ( xy – 1 ) dx = 0, x > 0,$~$y  \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) =3 - e$. Then $y \left(1\right)$ \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is

$x^{3}dy + \left(xy - 1\right)dx = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 - xy}{x3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{x3} - \dfrac{y}{x2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x2} = \dfrac{1}{x3}$

This is a linear differential equation.

If~$IF = e^{∫ \dfrac{1}{x2}dx} = e^{- \dfrac{1}{x}}$

Solution of a given~linear differential equation is

$ye^{- \dfrac{1}{x}} = ∫ e^{- \dfrac{1}{x}}\left(\dfrac{1}{x3}\right)dx$

Put~$- \dfrac{1}{x} = t ⇒ \dfrac{dx}{x2} = dt$

$⇒ ye^{- \dfrac{1}{x}} = - ∫ e^{- t}tdt$

$⇒ ye^{- \dfrac{1}{x}} = te^{- t} + e^{- t} + C$

$⇒ y = t + 1 + Ce\dfrac{1}{x}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{1}{x} + 1 + Ce\dfrac{1}{x}$

Put~$x = \dfrac{1}{2}$, then~

$3 - e = 2 + 1 + Ce^{2}$

$C = - \dfrac{1}{e}$

So,

$y = \dfrac{1}{x} + 1 - \dfrac{1}{e} \left($e$\dfrac{1}{x}\right)

So,

$y\left($1\right) = 1 + 1 - 1 = 1$

questions.q: Let $y = y  \left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation ${cosec}^{2}xdy + 2dx = \left(1 + ycos2x\right){cosec}^{2}xdx,$~with~$y\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) =0 .$~Then, the value of \l$left(y\left($0\right) + 1\right)2$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& ${cosec}^{2}xdy + 2dx = \left(1 + ycos2x\right){cosec}^{2}xdx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{\sin^{2}x} + 2dx = \left(\dfrac{1 + ycos2x}{\sin^{2}x}\right)dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2\sin^{2}x = 1 + ycos2x$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2\sin^{2}x - 1 = ycos2x$

Using,~$cos2x = 1 - 2\sin^{2}x,$~we get

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(- cos2x\right) = ycos2x$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(- cos2x\right)y = cos2x$

This is a linear differential equation of the type~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$~where~$P \text{ and } Q$~are the functions of~$x$~or constants.

Thus,~$P = - cos2x \text{ and } Q = cos2x$

Now, we have integrating factor I.F.$= e^{∫ Pdx} = e^{∫ - cos2xdx} = e^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)}$

And, the solution of the given differential equation is

$y\left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q\left(I . F .\right)dx + c$

~$⇒ y \cdot e^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = ∫ \left(cos2x\right) \cdot e^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)}dx + c$

Put~$\dfrac{sin2x}{2} = t, ⇒ \dfrac{2cos2x}{2}dx = dt$

$⇒ y \cdot e^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = ∫ e^{- t}dt + c$

$⇒ y \cdot e^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = - e^{- t}dt + c$

$⇒ y \cdot e^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = - e^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} + c$

Given,~$y\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = 0$

$⇒ 0 \cdot e^{- \left(\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)}{2}\right)} = - e^{- \left(\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)}{2}\right)} + c$

$⇒ c = - e^{- \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}$

$⇒ y \cdot e^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = - e^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} + e^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

Now, at~$x = 0$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) \cdot e^{- \left(\dfrac{sin0}{2}\right)} = - e^{- \left(\dfrac{sin0}{2}\right)} + e^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) \cdot e^{0} = - e^{0} + e^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) = - 1 + e^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) + 1 = e^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ \left(y\left(0\right) + 1\right)2 = e^{- 1} .$

questions.q: $If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2ytanx = sinx, 0 < x < \dfrac{π}{2}$~and $y  \left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) =0$, then the maximum value of $y \left(x\right)$ \text{ and } is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\left(2tanx\right) = sinx$~is a linear differential equation so,

$I . F = e^{∫ 2tanxdx} = e^{2ln\left|secx\right|} = \sec^{2}x$

The general solution will be~

$y\sec^{2}x = ∫ sinx\sec^{2}xdx + C$

$⇒ y\sec^{2}x = secx + C$

$∵ y\left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) = 0 ⇒ C = - 2$

Hence the particular solution is

$y\sec^{2}x = secx - 2$

$⇒ y = cosx - 2\cos^{2}x$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{1}{8} - 2 \left(cosx - $\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$2$

So, the maximum value of y \left($x\right)$ is $\dfrac{1}{8}$

questions.q: If a curve passes through the origin and the slope of the tangent to it at any point  \left(x, y\right)$~is $\dfrac{x^{2} - 4x + y + 8}{x - 2},$& then this curve also passes through the point:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given

$y\left(0\right) = 0$

and~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\left(x - 2\right)2 + y + 4}{x - 2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y}{x - 2} = \left(x - 2\right) + \dfrac{4}{x - 2}$

$⇒ I . F . = e^{- ∫ \dfrac{1}{x - 2}dx} = \dfrac{1}{x - 2}$

Solution of L.D.E.

$⇒ y\dfrac{1}{x - 2} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{x - 2}\left(\left(x - 2\right) + \dfrac{4}{x - 2}\right) \cdot dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{x - 2} = x - \dfrac{4}{x - 2} + C$

Now, at~$x = 0, y = 0 ⇒ C = - 2$

$y = x \left(x - 2\right) - 4 - 2 \left($x - 2\right)$

$⇒ y = x^{2} - 4x$

This curve passes through~ \left(5, 5\right)$

questions.q: Let $y = y  \left(x\right)$~be the solution of the differential equation~\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{\sqrt{2}y}{2\cos^{4}x - cos2x} =$xe^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}$cot2x\right)}, 0 < x < $\dfrac{π}{2}~with $y\$left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\pi2}{32}.~If y $\$left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\pi2}{18}e^{- \tan^{- $1}  \left(\alpha\right)}$, then the value of $3{α}^{2}$ \text{ and } is equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{2}{2\cos^{4}x - cos2x}y = xe^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}$

This is a linear differential equation.

Here~$I = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{2\cos^{4}x - cos2x} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\cos^{2}2x}{2} + cos2x\right) - cos2x}$

$= 2\sqrt{2} ∫ \dfrac{\sec^{2}2xdx}{2 + \tan^{2}2x}$

Put~$tan2x = t$

$I = \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{tan2x}{2}$

$∴ IF = e^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{tan2x}{2}\right)} = e^{\cot^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}$

So general solution will be

$ye^{\cot^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)} = ∫ xe^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}e^{\cot^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}dx$

$ye^{\cot^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)} = e\dfrac{π}{2}\left(\dfrac{x2}{2}\right) + c$

$y\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{\pi2}{32} ⇒ c = 0$

i.e.~$y = \dfrac{x2}{2}e^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot2x\right)}$

Given~$y\left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\pi2}{18}e^{- \tan^{- 1}\alpha}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\pi2}{18}e^{- \tan^{- 1}\alpha} = \dfrac{\pi2}{18}e^{\tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{2}cot\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}= \dfrac{\pi2}{18}e^{- \tan^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}\right)}$

Hence~$\alpha = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}} ⇒ 3{α}^{2} = 2$

questions.q: For a differentiable function $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$, suppose $f^{\prime}(x)=3 f(x)+\alpha$, where $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, $f(0)=1$ and $\lim _{x \rightarrow-\infty} f(x)=7$. Then $9 f  \left(-\log _{\mathrm{e}}3\right) is equal to_________$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{d y}{d x}-3 y=\alpha \\ & \text { If }=e^{\int-3 d x}=e^{-3 x} \\ & \therefore \quad y-e^{-3 x}=\int e^{-3 x} \cdot \alpha d x \\ & y e^{-3 x}=\frac{\alpha e^{-3 x}}{-3}+c \\ & \left(* e^{3 x}\right) \\ & y=\frac{\alpha}{-3}+C \cdot e^{3 x}\end{aligned}$
on substituting $\mathrm{x}=0, \mathrm{y}=1x \rightarrow-\infty, y=7$
we get $y=7-6 e^{3 x}9 f\left(-\log _e 3\right)=61$

questions.q:
Let $y = y ( x )$ be solution of the following differential equation~

$e^{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2e^{y}sinx + sinx\cos^{2}x = 0, y \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) =$0$.

If $y\left($0\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\alpha + \betae^{- 2}\right), then $4 ( \alpha + \beta )$is equal to \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } .

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $e^{y} = t ⇒ e^{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dt}{dx}$

So,

$e^{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2e^{y}sinx + sinx\cos^{2}x = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dx} - \left(2sinx\right)t = - sinx\cos^{2}x$

So, the integrating factor~$I . F . = e^{∫ - 2sinxdx} = e^{2cosx}$

So, the solution of differential equation is~

$t \cdot e^{2cosx} = ∫ e^{2cosx} \cdot \left(- sinx\cos^{2}x\right)dx$

$⇒ e^{y} \cdot e^{2cosx} = ∫ e^{2z} \cdot z^{2}dz$~ (Assume,~$z = cosx ⇒ dz = - sinx$)

Using integration by parts,

$⇒ e^{y} \cdot e^{2cosx} = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot z^{2} \cdot e^{2z} - \dfrac{1}{2}z \cdot e^{2z} + \dfrac{e2z}{4} + C$

$⇒ e^{y} \cdot e^{2cosx} = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \cos^{2}x \cdot e^{2cosx} - \dfrac{1}{2}cosx \cdot e^{2cosx} + \dfrac{e2cosx}{4} + C$

at $x = \dfrac{π}{2}, y = 0 ⇒ C = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ e^{y} = \dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{2}x - \dfrac{1}{2}cosx + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4} \cdot e^{- 2cosx}$

Put~$x = 0$

$⇒ y = log\left[\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}e^{- 2}\right] ⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{1}{4}, \beta = \dfrac{3}{4}$

So,~$\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4} = 1$

questions.q: Let $f$ be a differentiable function such that $2(x+2)^2 f(x)-3(x+2)^2=10 \int_0^x(t+2) f(t) d t, x \geq 0$. Then $f(2)$ is equal to ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$2(x+2)^2 f(x)-3(x+2)^2=10 \int_0^x(t+2) f(t) d t$
Differentiating both side
$\begin{aligned}
& 4(x+2) f(x)+2 f(x)(x+2)^2-6(x+2)=10(x+2) f(x) \\
& =(x+2) \frac{d y}{d x}-3 y=3 \\
& \frac{1}{3} \int \frac{d y}{y+1}=\int \frac{d x}{x+2} \\
& \ln |y+1=3 \ln | x+2 \mid+\ln c \\
& y+1=(x+2)^3 c \\
& \because y(0)=\frac{3}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{5}{16}=c \\
& \therefore \quad y=\frac{5}{16}(x+2)^3-1 \\
& y(2)=\frac{5}{16} \times 64-1=19
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $x = x  \left(t\right)$ is the solution of the differential equation  \left(t + 1\right)dx = \left(2x + \left(t + 1\right)4\right)dt, x\left(0\right) = 2$, then $x\left(1\right) equals ________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: \left(t + 1\right)dx = \left(2x + \left($t + 1\right)4\right)dt$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dx}{dt} =$2x + \left($t + 1\right)4\left(t + 1\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dx}{dt} --2x\left(t + 1\right) = \left(t + 1\right)3$

$⇒ IF = e^{∫ \dfrac{- 2}{t + 1}dt}$

$⇒ IF = e^{- 2log\left|t + 1\right|}$

$⇒ IF = \dfrac{1}{\left(t + 1\right)2}$

Solution of the differential equations is given by,

$⇒ x \times \dfrac{1}{\left(t + 1\right)2} =∫ \left(t + 1\right)dt$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{\left(t + 1\right)2} = \dfrac{t2}{2} +t + c$

It is given that $x\left(0\right) = 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{\left(0 + 1\right)2} = \dfrac{0}{2} +0 + c$

$⇒ c = 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{\left(t + 1\right)2} = \dfrac{t2}{2} +t + 2$

Putting $t = 1$,

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{\left(1 + 1\right)2} = \dfrac{12}{2} +1 + 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2} +3$

$⇒ x = 2 + 12$

$⇒ x = 14

$
